mainTopic: The end of the בכור discussion, then the ברייתא listing what א׳ ניסן is the new year for: months, leap years, and תרומת שקלים.
overview: This amud opens by finishing a discussion from the previous amud. The second statement of אביי, that a בכור's year is counted from birth, refers to a בעל מום that is known to be full term. Next the גמרא quotes a ברייתא: א׳ ניסן is the new year for months, for leap years, and for תרומת שקלים, and some say also for renting houses. For 'months,' the proofs from the תורה (אביב and אסיף) fall apart, so רבינא and other אמוראים prove from נביאים and כתובים that ניסן is the first month. For 'leap years,' רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that ניסן is the deadline after which a leap year can no longer be declared. Along the way the גמרא explains the dispute over whether the deadline is פורים or the end of אדר. For the שקלים, רבי יאשיה learns from 'לחדשי השנה' and a גזירה שוה that the offerings are bought from the new funds starting in ניסן. שמואל and a ברייתא add that using old funds is still valid, and that an individual may donate a public offering if he hands it over to the community. The amud ends in the middle of the גמרא's answer to why that last rule needed to be said, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Counting from birth applies to a blemished firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. The statement of אביי that we count the year of a בכור from its birth refers to a בעל מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: That statement (count from birth) is about a blemished animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer that began in the previous section. It explains that the 'count from birth' statement refers to a בכור that has a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unblemished בכור cannot be brought as a קרבן until its eighth day, so its year is counted from then. A בעל מום is not a קרבן; it is simply eaten by the כהן. So it is ready from the day it is born, and the year (for the איסור of בל תאחר) starts at birth.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a blemish, which disqualifies it from being a קרבן
This one (pointing to one of two statements)
A firstborn animal that must be given to the כהן

phrases.english: That one is about a blemished animal.
phrases.notes: The second half of 'הא בתם, הא בבעל מום'; the first half appeared in the previous section.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the resolution of the contradiction between two statements of אביי that was raised in the previous section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each statement refers to a different kind of animal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two statements of אביי seemed to contradict each other about when the year of a בכור begins.
steps.terutzMaskana: An unblemished בכור is counted from the eighth day. A blemished בכור is counted from birth.

steps.title: Can a blemished animal be eaten on its day of birth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. Even a בעל מום should need to wait eight days, to make sure it is not a נפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can a blemished animal really be eaten right away?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It asks how a blemished animal could be eaten on the very day it is born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we wait eight days after any animal is born, in case it is a נפל that will not survive. If so, even a בעל מום would not be ready at birth. That would undo the claim that its year starts at birth.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about whether a בעל מום may be eaten at all; it may. The question is only about timing: can it be eaten on the day it is born, before eight days have passed?

phrases.aramaic: בַּעַל מוּם מִי מָצֵי אָכֵיל לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: Can one really eat a blemished animal (on the day it is born)?
phrases.notes: Assumed background: a newborn animal is treated as a possible נפל until its eighth day.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעַל מוּם מִי מָצֵי אָכֵיל לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case setting proposed in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a בעל מום is ready to be eaten from birth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every newborn animal may be a נפל and needs eight days. So the year should not start at birth even for a בעל מום.

steps.title: When we know the pregnancy was full term
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is one where we know the animal's months of pregnancy were complete, so it is not a נפל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he knows for sure that its months of pregnancy were completed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its answer. It limits the case to an animal that we know was born after a full pregnancy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eight-day wait exists only because we are unsure whether the animal is viable. If we know when it was conceived and that the pregnancy went full term, there is no doubt. Then the בעל מום may be eaten at once, and its year starts at birth.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clearly known to him
Its months of pregnancy were completed
A premature birth that is not viable

steps.whatToRemember: An unblemished בכור is counted from day eight. A blemished בכור that is known to be full term is counted from its birth.

phrases.english: Where it is clearly known to him about it
phrases.notes: For example, he saw when the mother conceived.

phrases.english: that its months (of pregnancy) were completed.
phrases.notes: So it is not a נפל and needs no eight-day wait.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּקִים לֵיהּ בֵּיהּ שֶׁכָּלוּ לוֹ חֳדָשָׁיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: a known full-term birth.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every newborn needs eight days because it might be a נפל.
steps.terutzMaskana: When we know the pregnancy was full term, there is no doubt of נפל, so the animal is ready at birth.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists what א׳ ניסן is the new year for
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds to the משנה. א׳ ניסן is the new year for months, for leap years, and for תרומת שקלים. יש אומרים: also for renting houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: א׳ ניסן is the new year for months, for leap years, and for the collection of שקלים. Some say: also for the renting of houses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a ברייתא listing more things for which א׳ ניסן begins the year, beyond what the משנה said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said א׳ ניסן is the new year for kings and for רגלים. This ברייתא adds four more items. The גמרא will now go through them one by one and find a source or reason for each.

keyTerms.meaning: Leap years (adding a month to the year)
Taking from the half-shekel funds to buy communal קרבנות
Some say (a dissenting or additional opinion)

steps.whyThisMatters: This list sets the plan for the next part of the sugya. Each item will be explained in turn, starting with 'months'.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
On the first of Nisan is the new year
for months, and for leap years,
phrases.notes: 'Months' means we count the months starting from ניסן.

phrases.english: and for the collection of shekels.
phrases.notes: From ניסן, communal קרבנות are bought with the new year's funds.

phrases.english: And some say:
also for the renting of houses.
phrases.notes: Someone who rents a house 'for this year' rents it until ניסן.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּאֶחָד בְּנִיסָן רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לָחֳדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. It leaves the בכור discussion and returns to the list of new years.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: א׳ ניסן is the new year for months, leap years, and תרומת שקלים; according to יש אומרים, also for renting houses.

steps.title: What is the source for months?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that ניסן is the new year for counting months.
steps.simpleTranslation: For months, from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins working through the ברייתא's list, starting with the first item. It asks for a source, setting up the proof that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא stated the rule but gave no reason. The גמרא wants a פסוק showing that ניסן is the first month.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: For months, from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first item in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that the months are counted from ניסן.

steps.title: The verse calls the פסח month the first month
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes שמות יב. 'This month' is the first of the months, and it is the month of the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'This month shall be to you the beginning of months; it is the first of the months of the year for you. Speak to the whole congregation of Israel, saying: On the tenth of this month each man shall take a lamb for his father's house, a lamb per household. And it shall be kept by you until the fourteenth day of this month, and they shall slaughter it, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. It says the first month of the year is the month in which the קרבן פסח is offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק clearly says there is a 'first month'. But it does not name ניסן; it only says 'this month', the one with the קרבן פסח. That is why a second פסוק will be needed to identify which month it is.

keyTerms.meaning: The head, or beginning, of the months
A lamb or kid (the קרבן פסח)

phrases.english: As it is written: 'This month shall be to you
the beginning of months;
it is the first for you of the months of the year.
phrases.notes: The key words: there is a 'first month'.

phrases.aramaic: דַּבְּרוּ אֶל כׇּל עֲדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר
phrases.english: Speak to the whole congregation of Israel, saying:
On the tenth of this month
they shall take for themselves, each man, a lamb
for each father's house, a lamb per household.
And it shall be kept by you

phrases.aramaic: עַד אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר יוֹם לַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה
phrases.english: until the fourteenth day of this month
and they shall slaughter it, etc.'
phrases.notes: This shows that 'this month' is the month of the קרבן פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first half of the answer to the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The month of the קרבן פסח is called the first month.

steps.title: The month of ripening is ניסן, and it is called first
steps.stepSummary: A second פסוק says the פסח month is 'the month of אביב' (ripening grain). That can only be ניסן. So ניסן is the 'first month'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'Keep the month of ripening.' Which month has ripening grain? You must say: this is ניסן. And the תורה calls it 'first'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second פסוק to finish the proof. It identifies the 'first month' as ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק said the פסח month is 'first' but did not name it. The second פסוק says פסח falls in 'the month of אביב', when the grain ripens, and that is ניסן. Putting the two together: ניסן is the first month, so months are counted from it.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of ripening (when the barley ripens)
You must say (it can only be this)

steps.whatToRemember: Proof for 'months': the פסח month is called 'first' (שמות), and the פסח month is the month of אביב, which is ניסן (דברים). So ניסן is the first month.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'Keep the month of ripening',
phrases.notes: דברים טז:א, which goes on to say 'and make the פסח'.

phrases.english: Which month has ripening grain in it?
You must say: this is Nisan,
and the Torah calls it 'first'.
phrases.notes: This links back to 'it is the first for you' in the first פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 6 by identifying which month is 'first'.
steps.raayaObject: That א׳ ניסן is the new year for months.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות יב:ב–ו together with דברים טז:א (חודש האביב).

steps.title: Maybe the ripening month is אייר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the אביב proof: maybe the 'month of אביב' is אייר, not ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is אייר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in the last proof. Maybe the 'month of ripening' is אייר, the month after ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 assumed only ניסן fits the label 'month of אביב.' If אייר could also fit, the proof no longer points only to ניסן. Then אייר would be 'first,' and the count would shift.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (maybe it is something else)

phrases.english: But say it is Iyar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the identification of the אביב month as ניסן
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only ניסן is the 'month of אביב'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another nearby month might also be called the ripening month

steps.title: אייר has no ripening left
steps.stepSummary: The verse needs a month when ripening happens. In אייר the grain has already ripened.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need ripening, and there is none in אייר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אייר cannot be the 'month of אביב,' because by אייר the grain is already ripe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אביב' means grain in the middle of ripening. In אייר that stage has already passed. So אייר does not fit the label.

phrases.english: We need ripening, and there is none.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the אייר challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אייר might count as the ripening month
steps.terutzMaskana: In אייר the grain is already ripe, so it is not 'אביב'

steps.title: Maybe the ripening month is אדר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now suggests אדר, when some grain starts to ripen.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is אדר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the month before ניסן instead. Some ripening already starts in אדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ripening begins in אדר, then אדר also has אביב. In that case the verse might mean אדר, and the proof for ניסן would fail.

phrases.english: But say it is Adar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge, from the other side of ניסן
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only ניסן is the 'month of אביב'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Some ripening happens in אדר, so אדר could fit the verse

steps.title: אדר lacks most of the ripening
steps.stepSummary: The verse needs the month with most of the ripening, and that is not אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need most of the ripening, and that is not in אדר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'month of אביב' must be the month when most grain ripens. That is ניסן, not אדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא adds a new requirement: 'majority of ripening.' A little ripening in אדר is not enough to earn the name.

phrases.english: We need most of the ripening, and there is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the אדר challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any ripening qualifies a month as אביב
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the month of most ripening qualifies

steps.title: The verse never says 'most of the ripening'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer, because the verse only says 'אביב,' not 'most of אביב.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Is 'most of the ripening' written in the verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down its own answer. The פסוק does not say 'most,' so אדר is still possible, and the אביב proof fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'majority' requirement was added by us and is not in the text. Without it, אדר also has some אביב. So the verse cannot prove ניסן is first.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it at all...? (a rhetorical challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is phrased as a question, but it is not asking for information. It is rejecting the answer in step 11. Because of it, the whole אביב proof is dropped.

phrases.english: Is 'most of the ripening' written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 11, which brings down the step-7 proof
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire אביב proof that ניסן is first
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'majority' requirement is not in the פסוק

steps.title: רב חסדא: תשרי, the gathering month, is called 'seventh'
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא proves it from סוכות: the month of gathering crops is תשרי, and the תורה calls it 'seventh,' so ניסן is first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חסדא said: from here. 'On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you gather the crops of the land.' Which month has gathering? תשרי. And the תורה calls it 'seventh.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the אביב proof failed, רב חסדא brings a new proof. The month of gathering is תשרי, and the תורה calls it the 'seventh month.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תשרי is the seventh month, then counting back six months makes ניסן the first. This time the proof works from the autumn harvest instead of the spring ripening.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Chisda said: from here:
'But on the fifteenth day
of the seventh month,
when you gather the produce of the land.'
Which month has gathering in it?
You must say: this is Tishrei,
and it calls it 'seventh.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא כג:לט

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected אביב proof with a new source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that ניסן is first of the months (step 5)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תשרי, the month of gathering, is called 'seventh,' so ניסן is first

steps.title: Maybe the 'seventh' month is מרחשון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the verse means מרחשון, counted as seventh from אייר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is מרחשון, and 'seventh' means seventh from אייר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא the same way it challenged the אביב proof. Maybe the gathering month is מרחשון, and the count starts from אייר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מרחשון were the 'seventh,' the first month would be אייר, not ניסן. So the proof would not be conclusive.

phrases.english: But say it is Marcheshvan,
and what is 'seventh'? Seventh from Iyar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's identification of the month as תשרי
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only תשרי is the gathering month
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A later month could be 'seventh' if counted from אייר

steps.title: מרחשון has no gathering
steps.stepSummary: The verse needs gathering, and by מרחשון the crops are already in.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need gathering, and there is none in מרחשון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the gathering is already finished by מרחשון, so it cannot be the month the פסוק means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors the אייר answer in step 9. Once the gathering is over, the month no longer fits 'when you gather.'

phrases.english: We need gathering, and there is none.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מרחשון challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מרחשון might be the gathering month
steps.terutzMaskana: Gathering is already over in מרחשון

steps.title: Maybe the 'seventh' month is אלול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests אלול, when gathering begins, counted as seventh from אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is אלול, and 'seventh' means seventh from אדר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the month before תשרי. Gathering starts in אלול, and אלול is seventh if you count from אדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this were right, אדר would be the first month instead of ניסן. It parallels the אדר challenge in step 10.

phrases.english: But say it is Elul,
and what is 'seventh'? Seventh from Adar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge, from the other side of תשרי
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only תשרי is the gathering month
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Some gathering happens in אלול, so אלול could fit

steps.title: אלול lacks most of the gathering
steps.stepSummary: The verse needs the month with most of the gathering, and that is תשרי, not אלול.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need most of the gathering, and that is not in אלול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the same 'majority' idea it used for אדר. Most gathering happens in תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some gathering in אלול is not enough. Only the month with most of the gathering earns the name.

phrases.english: We need most of the gathering, and there is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the אלול challenge
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the month of most gathering qualifies

steps.title: The verse never says 'most of the gathering'
steps.stepSummary: The 'majority' answer fails again, because the פסוק only says 'gathering.' רב חסדא's proof falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is 'most of the gathering' written in the verse?
steps.whatsHappening: Just as in step 12, the גמרא rejects the 'majority' answer. So אלול remains possible, and רב חסדא's proof does not stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both proofs from the תורה fail for the same reason. A farming description fits more than one month unless we add 'majority,' and the פסוק does not say that.

phrases.english: Is 'most of the gathering' written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 17, which brings down רב חסדא's proof
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב חסדא's entire proof from אסיף
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'majority' requirement is not in the פסוק

steps.title: רבינא: Proof from זכריה, שבט is the eleventh month
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says we cannot learn this from the תורה, only from נביאים: זכריה calls שבט the eleventh month.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבינא said: we did not learn this from the תורה of משה רבינו. We learned it from דברי קבלה: 'On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is the month of שבט.'
steps.whatsHappening: After both proofs from the תורה fail, רבינא brings a verse from זכריה. It names the month and its number together: שבט is the eleventh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here no farming clue is needed, so there is nothing to argue about. If שבט is eleventh, then counting back makes ניסן the first.

keyTerms.meaning: נביאים and כתובים (the later books of תנ״ך)

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא openly admits that this point is not proven from the חומש, only from נביאים. That is an unusual and honest conclusion.

phrases.english: Rather, Ravina said:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר זֶה מִתּוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לֹא לָמַדְנוּ,
phrases.english: This matter we did not learn from the Torah of Moshe our teacher;
we learned it from the words of tradition (Prophets):
'On the twenty-fourth day
of the eleventh month,
which is the month of Shevat.'
phrases.notes: זכריה א:ז

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבִינָא, דָּבָר זֶה מִתּוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לֹא לָמַדְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed proofs from the תורה with an explicit verse in נביאים
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that ניסן is first of the months
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זכריה calls שבט the eleventh month, so ניסן is first

steps.title: רבה בר עולא: Proof from אסתר, טבת is the tenth month
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא brings a different verse from מגילת אסתר: טבת is called the tenth month.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא said: from here: 'And אסתר was taken to King אחשורוש, to his royal house, in the tenth month, which is the month of טבת.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives another explicit verse, from כתובים, that names a month together with its number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If טבת is the tenth month, counting back gives ניסן as first. It is the same kind of proof as רבינא's, just from a different book.
steps.whatToRemember: The תורה's farming clues (אביב, אסיף) fit more than one month, so they cannot prove that ניסן is first. The proof comes from נביאים and כתובים, which name the month and its number outright: שבט is the eleventh month (זכריה) and טבת is the tenth (אסתר).

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla said: from here:
'And Esther was taken to King Achashverosh
to his royal house
in the tenth month,
which is the month of Tevet.'
phrases.notes: אסתר ב:טז

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel alternative source alongside רבינא's
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that ניסן is first of the months
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אסתר calls טבת the tenth month, so ניסן is first

steps.title: רב כהנא's verse: כסלו is the ninth month
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא brings a verse from זכריה that calls כסלו the ninth month, which works only if we count from ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: We learn it from here: 'On the fourth day of the ninth month, in כסלו.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא offers his own verse to prove that the months of the year are counted from ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Count from ניסן and כסלו is the ninth month. Count from תשרי and it would be the third. The verse calls it the ninth, so the counting starts at ניסן.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: from here:
'On the fourth of the ninth month, in Kislev.'
phrases.notes: זכריה ז:א

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another alternate source alongside רבינא and רבה בר עולא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כסלו is called the ninth month, so the count starts from ניסן.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב's verse: סיון is the third month
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב brings a verse from אסתר that calls סיון the third month.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: From here: 'And the king's scribes were called at that time, in the third month, which is the month of סיון.'
steps.whatsHappening: A further אמורא gives a different verse proving the same point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting from ניסן, the months go ניסן, אייר, סיון, so סיון is third. The verse matches only that count.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said: from here:
'And the king's scribes were called at that time,
in the third month, which is the month of Sivan.'
phrases.notes: אסתר ח:ט

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds yet another source verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סיון is called the third month.

steps.title: רב אשי's verse: אדר is the twelfth month
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings the verse of the lottery (פור) before המן, which calls אדר the twelfth month.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: From here: 'He cast פור, which is the lot, before המן, from day to day and from month to month, to the twelfth month, which is the month of אדר.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא offers another verse from מגילת אסתר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אדר can be called the twelfth month only if we start counting at ניסן. Counting from תשרי, אדר would be sixth.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: from here:
'He cast pur, which is the lot, before Haman
from day to day and from month to month,
to the twelfth, which is the month of Adar.'
phrases.notes: אסתר ג:ז

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another source verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אדר is called the twelfth month.

steps.title: An unnamed option: ניסן is called the first month
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers the most direct-looking verse: 'In the first month, which is the month of ניסן.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it comes from here: 'In the first month, which is the month of ניסן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests one more verse, which seems to say plainly that ניסן is first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This verse looks the clearest of all, since it names ניסן as 'first.' That makes us wonder why the other אמוראים did not use it. The next step asks exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another option)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: from here:
'In the first month, which is the month of Nisan.'
phrases.notes: אסתר ג:ז

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final alternative source, taken from the same פסוק as רב אשי's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ניסן is explicitly called the first month.

steps.title: Why didn't the others use the ניסן verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why all the other אמוראים skipped the verse that calls ניסן 'first,' which seems the clearest proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them, what is the reason they did not say it comes from this verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the earlier אמוראים did not use the simple 'first month is ניסן' verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a verse openly calls ניסן 'first,' it seems to settle the question. So there must be a weakness in it that made the others look elsewhere.

phrases.english: And all of them, what is the reason
they did not say: from this one?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלְּהוּ, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמְרִי מֵהַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the step 24 verse was not used by the others.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the other אמוראים rejected the explicit ניסן verse.

steps.title: 'First' may mean first in its own story
steps.stepSummary: The word 'first' might mean only the first month of the המן story (when the lots began), not the first month of the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps what does 'first' mean? First for its own matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ניסן verse might not be talking about the calendar at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: המן started casting lots in ניסן, so ניסן could be 'first' only within that event. A number like 'twelfth' or 'ninth' cannot be explained that way, so those verses give a stronger proof.

keyTerms.meaning: For its own matter (in its own context)

steps.whatToRemember: The verse calling ניסן 'first' is weak, because 'first' may refer only to the lottery story. The numbered-month verses are stronger proofs.

phrases.english: Perhaps what does 'first' mean?
First for its own matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'First' may mean first in the lottery event, not first of the year.

steps.title: What about the תנא of our משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why our משנה does not list ניסן as ראש השנה for months, the way the ברייתא does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question: why did the author of our משנה leave out 'ראש השנה for months'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists ניסן as ראש השנה for months, but our משנה does not. The גמרא wants to know the reason for the gap.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא (the author of our משנה)

phrases.english: And our tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the source for months to the wording of our משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why our משנה omits ראש השנה for months.

steps.title: Our משנה deals with years, not months
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה lists only new years for things counted in years. The order of the months is a different subject.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is dealing with years; he is not dealing with months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that our משנה's topic is years, so a 'new year for months' does not belong in its list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item in the משנה is a start date for counting years, such as years of kings or festivals. The order of the months is not a count of years, so the משנה left it out.

phrases.english: He is dealing with years;
he is not dealing with months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה covers only counts of years.

steps.title: Do we really count leap years from ניסן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's next item, 'and for leap years,' and asks whether leap years are truly counted from ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And for leap years.' Do we really count leap years from ניסן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: the ברייתא's statement that ניסן is ראש השנה for leap years. It challenges that statement, and the proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said ניסן is ראש השנה for עיבורין (leap years). The גמרא doubts this and is about to bring a source that seems to tie leap years to תשרי and אדר instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Leap years (years given an extra month)

phrases.english: 'And for leap years.'
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא

phrases.english: Do we count leap years from Nisan?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New section on the ברייתא's item about leap years.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that ניסן is ראש השנה for leap years.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A leap-year declaration seems to depend on תשרי, not ניסן (proven in the next step).

steps.title: ברייתא: leap years are declared only after ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a leap year may not be declared before ראש השנה, and if needed it can be declared right after ראש השנה. Even then, only אדר is added.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: We do not declare a leap year before ראש השנה, and if they did, it is not a leap year. But under pressing conditions, they may declare it right after ראש השנה. Even so, they add only אדר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as proof for its challenge. The ברייתא connects declaring a leap year to ראש השנה in תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The declaration depends on whether ראש השנה (תשרי) has passed, which suggests the leap-year 'year' begins in תשרי. Also, the extra month is always a second אדר. So in what way is ניסן the new year for leap years? The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not make a leap year
But it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Declaring the leap year and adding the month are two separate things. The court may decide in תשרי, but the extra month itself is always a second אדר, added at the end of the year just before ניסן.

phrases.english: But it was taught: we do not intercalate the year
before Rosh Hashanah,
and if they intercalated it, it is not intercalated.
But due to pressing circumstances,

phrases.aramaic: מְעַבְּרִין אוֹתָהּ אַחַר רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה מִיָּד.
phrases.english: they intercalate it immediately after Rosh Hashanah.
And even so,
they add only Adar.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין הַשָּׁנָה לִפְנֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the step 29 challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That leap years are not counted from ניסן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא tying the leap-year declaration to after ראש השנה in תשרי, with only אדר added.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's coming explanation of what 'ראש השנה for leap years' in ניסן really means.

steps.title: Leap years means the deadline for adding a month
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that 'ראש השנה for leap years' means ניסן is the cutoff point after which a leap year can no longer be declared.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What does 'for leap years' mean? It means the stopping point for declaring leap years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from steps 29-30. ניסן is not where leap years start. It is the deadline for declaring them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the ברייתא meant leap years are counted from ניסן. רב נחמן בר יצחק reads the word differently: ניסן marks when declaring stops. Once ניסן begins, the בית דין can no longer add a second אדר to the year.

keyTerms.meaning: Leap years, meaning years where an extra month is added

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think ניסן begins a new leap-year cycle. ניסן is the END point. After it arrives, the year that just passed can no longer become a leap year.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
What is meant by 'leap years'?
The cutoff of declaring leap years.
phrases.notes: Once ניסן comes, the year can no longer be made a leap year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מַאי עִיבּוּרִין — הַפְסָקַת עִיבּוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge raised in steps 29-30
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leap years are counted from ניסן
steps.terutzMaskana: ניסן is the deadline after which a leap year can no longer be declared

steps.title: Proof that the deadline is the end of אדר
steps.stepSummary: A משנה records testimony that a leap year can be declared all through אדר, against those who said only until פורים. This shows ניסן is the cutoff.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: They testified that a leap year may be declared all through אדר, because there were some who said: only until פורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove there is a deadline for declaring a leap year. By the view accepted in the testimony, the deadline is the end of אדר, which means ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views agree there is a deadline. The disagreement is only whether it is פורים or the end of אדר. The testimony says all of אדר, so the moment ניסן arrives, no more adding is allowed. This supports רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
They make the year a leap year
The holiday on the 14th of אדר

phrases.english: As we learned: They testified
phrases.notes: 'They' are רבי יהושע and רבי פפייס, in a משנה in עדיות.

phrases.english: that one may make the year a leap year all through אדר.
For there were those who said: only until פורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הֵן הֵעִידוּ שֶׁמְּעַבְּרִין הַשָּׁנָה כׇּל אֲדָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 31 with a source
steps.raayaObject: That ניסן is the deadline for declaring a leap year
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה recording the testimony of רבי יהושע and רבי פפייס

steps.title: Why would some limit the deadline to פורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the view that a leap year may be declared only until פורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the one who said: only until פורים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to understand the stricter view in the משנה. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave two deadlines but no reasons. The גמרא wants to know why פורים would matter for setting the calendar.

phrases.english: What is the reason of the one who said
'only until פורים'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר עַד הַפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind one opinion in the proof source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the deadline would be פורים

steps.title: After פורים people start preparing for פסח
steps.stepSummary: From פורים, people begin learning the laws of פסח, 30 days early. Pushing פסח off a month after that could make people careless about חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the Master said: One asks about the laws of פסח thirty days before פסח. If they then add a month, people will come to treat חמץ lightly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the פורים view. פורים is 30 days before פסח, when people start getting ready, so a late change could cause confusion about חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פורים falls on 14 אדר. Right after it, on 15 אדר, it is exactly 30 days before פסח (15 ניסן), and people begin learning the laws of פסח. If the בית דין adds a month after that, people who were ready for פסח suddenly have it delayed. They might lose respect for the date and be careless about חמץ on the real פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: To treat lightly, to be careless about

phrases.english: Since the Master said:
One asks about the laws of פסח
thirty days before פסח,
phrases.notes: Thirty days before פסח is פורים.

phrases.english: people will come to treat חמץ lightly.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר מָר: שׁוֹאֲלִין בְּהִלְכוֹת הַפֶּסַח קוֹדֶם לַפֶּסַח שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After פורים people start preparing for פסח, so a delay could make them careless about חמץ

steps.title: The other view: people know the calendar depends on calculation
steps.stepSummary: Those who allow all of אדר say people know a leap year depends on calculations. They will assume the חכמים just finished calculating late, so they will not take פסח lightly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other opinion? It is well known that a leap year depends on calculation. People will think: the calculation was not completed by the חכמים until now.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the other side is not worried about the פורים problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows that a leap year depends on the חכמים' calculation. A late announcement will look like the calculation just took longer. People will not think the חכמים are playing with the dates, so they will still respect פסח and be careful with חמץ.

phrases.english: And the other opinion?
phrases.notes: The view of רבי יהושע and רבי פפייס, who allow all of אדר.

phrases.english: It is well known that a leap year
is a matter that depends on calculation,
and they will think: it is the calculation
that was not completed by the חכמים
until now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning of the opposing view, explaining why the concern of step 34 does not apply
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: People know the calendar depends on calculation, so a late leap year will not lead them to treat פסח lightly

steps.title: Why does our משנה leave out leap years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the main topic and asks why our משנה did not list ניסן as ראש השנה for leap years, as the ברייתא does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא? Why did he not mention it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back from the side discussion to the main issue. It asks why our משנה left out leap years, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that 'leap years' is explained as the ניסן cutoff, it seems like a real rule tied to ניסן. So why didn't our משנה include it among the things that start on ניסן?

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא, the author of our משנה

phrases.english: And our תנא? (Why did he leave it out?)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about פורים and returns to comparing our משנה with the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why our משנה does not list ניסן for leap years

steps.title: Our משנה lists only beginnings, not endings
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה lists only dates when something begins. For leap years, ניסן is an end point, so it is not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is dealing with beginnings. He is not dealing with endings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that our משנה counts only dates where a count starts. ניסן ends the chance to declare a leap year, so it does not belong on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every item in our משנה is a true 'new year', a point where counting begins. For leap years, ניסן marks when declaring stops. Since that is a stopping point, our תנא left it out. This matches step 28, where our משנה also left out the order of months because it was a different kind of subject.

keyTerms.meaning: He is dealing with, he is talking about

steps.whatToRemember: ניסן is called ראש השנה for leap years only in the sense that it is the deadline: after ניסן begins, no month can be added. Because this is an end point and not a beginning, our משנה does not list it.

phrases.english: He is dealing with beginnings,
he is not dealing with endings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Our משנה lists only starting points. For leap years, ניסן is an ending point.

steps.title: Where do we learn that ניסן starts the year for the שקלים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item in the ברייתא, ניסן as new year for תרומת שקלים, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ניסן is the new year for the collection of the שקלים. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up the next item from the ברייתא's list of new years and asks for its source. This sets up רבי יאשיה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each year the Jewish people give a half-שקל, and the money buys the public קרבנות. The ברייתא said this 'money year' renews in ניסן. The גמרא wants a פסוק that shows it.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking out the yearly half-שקל collection to buy public offerings
From where do we know this? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: And for the collection of the shekels.
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא's list of new years

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the side discussion about leap years, the גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's list and takes the next item.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that ניסן begins the year for the שקלים.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה: Renew the year and bring offerings from new money
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה reads 'לחדשי השנה' as 'renew' and bring offerings from the new collection. A גזירה שוה on 'שנה' shows that this renewal is in ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יאשיה said: The פסוק says, 'This is the burnt-offering of each month in its month, for the months of the year.' The תורה is saying: renew, and bring an offering from the new collection. And we learn 'year' from 'year' that it starts in ניסן, as it is written: 'It is the first for you of the months of the year.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יאשיה gives the source. He reads a פסוק to mean that each year the offerings must come from new money. Then he uses the word 'שנה' to show that this year starts in ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לחדשי' sounds like 'חדש', meaning 'renew'. So the תורה tells us to renew the money each year. But the פסוק does not say which month is the start. The word 'השנה' also appears in the ניסן פסוק ('ראשון הוא לכם'), so a גזירה שוה connects them.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn 'year' from 'year', a גזירה שוה from a shared word
'It is the first for you', the פסוק about ניסן

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate moves here. First the פסוק teaches that the money must be renewed every year. Only then does the גזירה שוה tell us when the renewal happens, which is ניסן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya said: The verse says:
"This is the burnt-offering of each month in its month
phrases.notes: במדבר כח:יד

phrases.english: for the months of the year"
phrases.notes: These seemingly extra words are the source

phrases.english: The Torah is saying: renew
phrases.notes: Wordplay: לחדשי read as חדש

phrases.english: and bring an offering from the new collection.
And we learn "year" from "year" that it is from Nisan,
as it is written: "It is the first for you
phrases.notes: שמות יב:ב

phrases.english: of the months of the year."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source in step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'לחדשי השנה' requires renewing the funds every year, and a גזירה שוה on 'שנה' with the ניסן פסוק sets the renewal in ניסן.

steps.title: Why not link the word 'year' to תשרי instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the word 'השנה' also appears in a פסוק about תשרי, so why not learn the renewal date from there?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us learn 'year' from 'year' from תשרי, as it is written: 'From the beginning of the year!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the גזירה שוה. The word 'שנה' also appears in a פסוק that refers to תשרי, so why choose ניסן?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה works through a shared word. The challenge is that 'השנה' shows up in two places that point to two different months. Without a reason to pick one, the proof for ניסן is weak.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From the beginning of the year', a פסוק understood to refer to תשרי

phrases.english: But let us learn "year" from "year" from Tishrei,
as it is written: "From the beginning of the year"!
phrases.notes: דברים יא:יב

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the גזירה שוה used in step 39.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of the ניסן פסוק for the גזירה שוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word 'השנה' also appears regarding תשרי, so the גזירה שוה could just as well point to תשרי.

steps.title: Compare a 'year with months' to another 'year with months'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that our פסוק mentions 'months' along with 'year', just like the ניסן פסוק. The תשרי פסוק does not mention months, so it is a weaker match.
steps.simpleTranslation: We compare a 'year' that has 'months' with it to a 'year' that has 'months' with it. We do not compare a 'year' that has 'months' with it to a 'year' that has no 'months' with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ניסן פסוק is the better match. Both פסוקים say 'לחדשי השנה', months together with year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source פסוק and the ניסן פסוק share two words, 'חדשי' and 'השנה'. The תשרי פסוק has only 'השנה'. The closer match wins, so the גזירה שוה points to ניסן.
steps.whatToRemember: The new year for the שקלים is ניסן. This comes from 'לחדשי השנה' (renew the funds yearly), linked by a גזירה שוה to the ניסן פסוק, which also says 'months of the year'.

phrases.english: We derive a "year" that has "months" with it
from a "year" that has "months" with it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין דָּנִין שָׁנָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמָּהּ חֳדָשִׁים
phrases.english: and we do not derive a "year" that has "months" with it
from a "year" that has no "months" with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּנִין שָׁנָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמָּהּ חֳדָשִׁים מִשָּׁנָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ עִמָּהּ חֳדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 40.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Better textual match: the shared words are stronger with ניסן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any פסוק with 'השנה' could serve for the גזירה שוה, including the תשרי one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ניסן פסוק shares both 'חדשי' and 'השנה', so it is the correct match.

steps.title: שמואל: ניסן offerings should come from new funds, but old funds still work
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that public offerings of ראש חודש ניסן ideally come from the new שקלים. If old funds were used, the offering is valid, but the extra מצוה was missed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Public offerings brought on the first of ניסן should, as a מצוה, be brought from the new collection. If one brought them from the old, he has fulfilled his obligation, but he missed the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a practical rule built on the source we just learned. Using new money in ניסן is the ideal way, not a requirement for validity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'renew' teaching could have been read as an absolute requirement. שמואל says it is only the best way to do the מצוה. The קרבן itself is valid with old money.

keyTerms.meaning: Public offerings, brought for the whole community
From the new funds / from the old funds

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the ניסן renewal is a לכתחילה rule. Breaking it does not invalidate the offering.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Public offerings that are brought on the first of Nisan —
it is a מצוה to bring them from the new collection.
And if he brought them from the old, he has fulfilled his obligation,
except that he lacked the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule of renewing funds in ניסן and defines how strict it is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Using new funds for ראש חודש ניסן offerings is a מצוה לכתחילה. Old funds are valid בדיעבד.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל word for word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the same ruling as שמואל, as support.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: Public offerings brought on the first of ניסן should, as a מצוה, be brought from the new collection. If one brought them from the old, he has fulfilled his obligation, but he missed the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא says exactly what שמואל said. This backs up his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תניא נמי הכי' is a support formula. It does not challenge anything. It shows that שמואל's ruling matches an earlier teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports the statement)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Public offerings that are brought on the first of Nisan —
it is a מצוה to bring them from the new collection,
and if he brought them from the old, he has fulfilled his obligation,
except that he lacked the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's statement from step 42.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that new funds are ideal and old funds are valid

steps.title: An individual may donate a public offering if he gives it to the community
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא adds that if an individual donates public offerings from his own money, they are valid, as long as he transfers them to the community.
steps.simpleTranslation: And an individual who donated them from his own property, they are valid, as long as he hands them over to the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a new point. A private person can pay for a public offering if he gives it fully to the community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Public offerings normally come from the community's שקלים. This clause allows private funding, but only if ownership passes to the public. That way it is still truly a קרבן צבור.

keyTerms.meaning: That he hands them over to the community

steps.whatToRemember: ניסן offerings should come from the new שקלים, but old funds are valid. A private donor may also fund them, as long as he gives them over to the community.

phrases.english: And an individual who volunteered them from his own, they are valid,
provided that he transfers them to the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא from step 43 continues with an additional ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Privately donated public offerings are valid if transferred to the community's ownership.

steps.title: Isn't this ruling obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: of course an individual may donate a public offering once he hands it over to the ציבור. Why say it at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is questioning the ruling from the last step. It says the rule is so obvious that the ברייתא should not have needed to state it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that if an individual pays for a קרבן ציבור, it is valid as long as he gives it over to the ציבור. Once it fully belongs to the community, it is a normal public offering, so the rule seems too simple to need saying. The גמרא assumes a ברייתא does not waste words on the obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. A challenge that a statement teaches nothing new.
A public offering, owned by the whole community

steps.confusionAlert: פשיטא is not saying the ruling is wrong. It agrees with the ruling and only asks why it needed to be said.

phrases.english: It is obvious!
phrases.notes: This refers to the ברייתא's ruling that an individual may donate, if he transfers it to the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ruling just quoted in step 44
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that an individual may donate a public offering if he transfers it to the ציבור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the animal fully belongs to the community, it is a normal public offering. So the ruling seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: We might have worried about something
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer: without this ruling, we might have thought we should worry that perhaps... (the worry is finished on the next amud).
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: we should be concerned that perhaps...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the 'obvious' question by showing a mistake we might have made. This line only sets up that mistake, and the rest of the sentence comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase מהו דתימא brings in a 'you might have thought' (a הוה אמינא), which shows why the ruling was needed. Here the possible mistake is a worry (ליחוש) about something that might go wrong when an individual donates. As the next passage shows, the worry is that he might not hand it over to the community properly.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. This introduces a possible wrong assumption that the ruling comes to reject.
Let us be concerned. Worry about a possible problem.

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. Do not stop at 'perhaps'. The actual worry, about whether he will transfer it properly, comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
phrases.notes: Opens the 'you might have thought' answer to the פשיטא.

phrases.english: we should be concerned that perhaps
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud, which says what the concern is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the פשיטא challenge of step 45
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a possible mistake (הוה אמינא) that the ruling comes to rule out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have worried that an individual donor would not properly transfer the offering to the ציבור, so his donation should not be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling teaches that we do not have this worry. The donation is valid once he transfers it. This conclusion appears on the next amud.
